SMTO-EXE-0227 — That Docker name matches more than one item

GUID: 800a06e4-c396-585b-a51d-239e0f2744c4
Slug: docker-container-ambiguous
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: docker

What happened

  • The name you gave matches more than one container, image, network or volume on the Gateway computer, so SMTO refused to guess which one you meant. Nothing was changed.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Ask SMTO to list the matching Docker items on that Gateway, showing their full IDs. Every item has its own full ID, even when names are shared; Docker networks, for example, can share a name.
  2. Decide which one you mean, then ask SMTO to act on it using its complete ID, not a shortened one. A complete ID points to exactly one item, and SMTO doesn't accept shortened IDs.

What success looks like

  • SMTO acts on the one item you chose, identified by its full ID.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages Docker on that computer. Don't remove the extra items just to make the name unique; they may belong to other work.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Exact Docker object resolution matched more than one distinct ID for the supplied name or tag (for example duplicate network names), so the Gateway refused to choose one.

What this means

  • Exact Docker object lookup found more than one distinct identity for the supplied name/tag and refused to choose one. Docker execution remains on the selected Gateway and its explicitly configured local Engine. Preserve accepted private references, exact object identities, completed prefixes and unknown effects; diagnostics never replay a mutation.

Why this can happen

  • Exact Docker object lookup found more than one distinct identity for the supplied name/tag and refused to choose one.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect matching full object IDs on the same Engine, not abbreviated prefixes.

How to fix it

  • Backend.exact found several distinct IDs for the value (typically Docker networks sharing a name, or a name equal to another object's ID). List the candidates with full IDs (docker network ls --no-trunc, docker ps -a --no-trunc) on the Gateway host and pass the intended complete ID.
  • Inspect matching objects and select the intended complete ID before another action.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect the exact object identity, typed arguments and selected Gateway capability; correct the reported prerequisite before a new request.

How to verify the fix

  • One deliberately chosen full identity resolves to the intended object.

What not to do

  • Never automatically replay an uncertain Docker mutation.

Technical notes

  • Docker execution remains on the selected Gateway and its explicitly configured local Engine. Preserve accepted private references, exact object identities, completed prefixes and unknown effects; diagnostics never replay a mutation.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
